answer: Each agent’s reputation can be tied to a vault-backed stake that is gradually released only after the identity completes useful work and survives random audits. A new identity therefore cannot instantly borrow the trust of an established one: it must lock real value, while coordinated agents risk losing stake when auditors detect duplicated behavior or fabricated results. The crystal-clear tradeoff is that a sybil attacker must fund every persona separately and keep that capital exposed over time; raising the attack’s scale raises its cost, even if the delta in reputation is slow to earn.
